questions.question: The compound interest (compounded annually) on a sum of money invested for two years is Rs. 10125. If the rate of interest is 25% per annum, then what is the amount after these two years?
questions.solution:
Given, compound interest = Rs. 10125, time = 2 years and rate = 25%

⇒ 10125 = p [(1 + 25/100)² – 1]

⇒ 10125 = p × [25/16 – 1]

⇒ p = 10125 × 16/9

⇒ p = 18000

⇒ The amount after two years = 18000 + 10125

∴ The amount after two years will be Rs. 28125

questions.question: A sum of money becomes double of itself in 50 months when invested on simple interest. What is the rate of interest per annum?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A sum of money becomes double of itself in 50 months

**Concept used:**

SI = PRT/100

A = SI + P

P → principal R → rate of interest T → time

**Calculation:**

Let principal = P

According to the question,

2p = p + (p × R × 50/1200)

⇒ p = p × R × 1/24

**∴ The rate percent is 24% **

questions.question: In a mixture of 60 litres, the ratio (by volume) of milk and water is 2 : 1. If X litres of water is added in the mixture, the ratio of milk and water becomes 1 : 2, then what is the value of X?
questions.solution:
The quantity of milk in the mixture = 60 × 2/3 = 40 litres

And the quantity of water in the mixture = 60 × 1/3 = 20 litres

According to question,

40/(20 + x) = 1/2

⇒ 20 + x = 80

⇒ x = 60

∴ The value of x is 60 litres.

questions.question: The speed of a boat in still water is 30 km/h. If the boat covers 60 km downstream in 1 hour 30 minutes, then what is the time taken by the boat to cover 60 km upstream?
questions.solution:
Let the speed of stream be a km/hour

So, the speed of boat in downstream = (30 + a) km/hour

And, the speed of boat in upstream = (30 – a) km/hour

According to the question,

60 = (30 + a) × 3/2

⇒ 30 + a = 40

⇒ a = 10 km/hour

So, the time taken by the boat to cover 60 km in upstream = 60/(30 – 10)

∴ Required time is 3 hours.

questions.question: Piyush alone can complete a work in 8 days and Arun alone can complete the same work in 14 days. If they both get Rs. 44000 to complete the work, then what is the share of Piyush?
questions.solution:
One day’s work of Piyush = 1/8

And one day’s work of Arun = 1/14

⇒ The efficiency ratio = 1/8 : 1/14 = 7 : 4

And we know that the efficiency ratio = wages ratio

⇒ The share of Piyush = 44000 × 7/11

∴ Piyush will get Rs. 28000

questions.question: The ratio of number of boys and girls in a school is 3 : 2. If there are 360 students in the school, then what is the number of girls in the school?
questions.solution:
Let the number of boys and girls in the school be 3x and 2x respectively

According to question,

3x + 2x = 360

⇒ 5x = 360

⇒ x = 72

∴ The number of girls in the school is 72 × 2 = 144

questions.question: Pipe D1 can fill an empty tank in 80 minutes and Pipe D2 can empty the same tank in 100 minutes. If pipes are opened simultaneously, then in how much time the tank gets completely filled?
questions.solution:
Since, D1 can fill 1/80 part of tanks in 1 minute

And D2 can empty 1/100 part of tank in 1 minute

⇒ (D1 + D2) together can fill (1/80 – 1/100) part of tank in 1 minute

∴ Together they will take 400 minutes to fill the tank.

questions.question: A room is in the shape of a cuboid, with dimensions of 12m × 10m × 3m. What is the cost of painting the four walls of the room at the rate of Rs. 50 per m²?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

TDimention of cuboid = 12m × 10m × 3m

**Formula used:**

Area of four walls of room = 2 (l + b) × h

**Calculation:**

⇒ The area of four walls of room = 2 (12 + 10) × 3 = 132 m²

So, the cost of the painting wall of the room = 132 × 50

**∴ The cost of painting the walls of the room is Rs. 6600**

questions.question: The average of six observations is 15. The average of first three among them is twice the average of the last three. What is the sum of the last three observations?
questions.solution:
Sum of all 6 observations = 15 × 6 = 90

Let the sum of last three observations is x

So, the sum of first three observations is (90 – x)

According to question,

The average of first three observations = 2 × The average of last three observations

(90 – x)/3 = 2 × x/3

⇒ 90 – x = 2x

⇒ x = 30

∴ The sum of last three numbers is 30.

questions.question: A bag contains 5 rupee, 2 rupee, 1 rupee and 50 paisa coins in the proportion 1 : 2 : 3 : 4. If the total amount in the bag is Rs. 168, then how many 50 paisa coins are there?
questions.solution:
Let the number of 5 rupee, 2 rupee, 1 rupee and 50 paisa coins are x, 2x, 3x and 4x respectively.

Now, according to question

5 × x + 2 × 2x + 1 × 3x + 1/2 × 4x = 168

⇒ 14x = 168

⇒ x = 12

∴ The number of 50 paisa coins is 12 × 4 = 48

questions.question: If Least Common Multiple of 23 and 24 is A, and Highest Common Factor of 23 and 24 is B. then what is the value of A + B?
questions.solution:
L.C.M of 23 and 24 = 552 (A)

And H.C.F of 23 and 24 = 1(B)

∴ A + B = 552 + 1 = 553
